featured.title: Gleisdreieck Berlin: The Station Where Two Lines Cross and the Park on Old Rail Land
featured.alt: Yellow U2 train on a steel viaduct at Gleisdreieck station in Berlin, with the station hall and a church spire behind
featured.summary: Start at Gleisdreieck U-Bahn station and walk through the park on the former rail yards. The route takes under an hour and points out the tracks and railway buildings along the way.
featured.label: Walk through Park am Gleisdreieck

miniPosts.title: Leipziger Platz Berlin: The Octagon Next to Potsdamer Platz and What to Look For
miniPosts.alt: A brightly painted slab of the inner Berlin Wall standing on the lawn of Leipziger Platz with glass towers behind it
miniPosts.summary: From Potsdamer Platz, step onto the eight-sided square and look for the painted wall slab. The guide shows what to look for if you have 15, 30 or 45 minutes.
miniPosts.label: Walk Leipziger Platz

miniPosts.title: Christmas Markets in Mitte: One Evening Walk, in the Order They Close
miniPosts.alt: The Alexanderplatz Christmas market at night, with a lit wooden Christmas pyramid and stalls under strings of lights
miniPosts.summary: Plan a walk from Alexanderplatz to Gendarmenmarkt around closing times. Check which stalls are open on your date before you set out from Hackescher Markt.
miniPosts.label: Plan an evening at the Mitte Christmas markets

miniPosts.title: Berlin U-Bahn Lines: Why the U1 to U4 Run Narrower Trains
miniPosts.alt: Yellow U2 train on the elevated viaduct at Bülowstraße in Berlin, between stone pylons with traffic below
miniPosts.summary: The U2 and U8 use different sizes of train. See which lines run narrower trains and what to look for on the U5 platforms.
miniPosts.label: Compare Berlin U-Bahn lines

miniPosts.title: Café Achteck Berlin: Where the Green Cast-Iron Toilets Still Stand
miniPosts.alt: Green octagonal cast-iron Café Achteck pavilion standing on a cobblestone island at Chamissoplatz in Berlin-Kreuzberg under summer trees
miniPosts.summary: Find the green cast-iron public toilets still standing in Moabit, Kreuzberg and Schöneberg. The map shows which ones you can see today.
miniPosts.label: Find a Café Achteck

posts.title: Where Was the Berlin Wall? An Interactive Map of East and West in 1989
posts.summary: The Berlin Wall ran 155 kilometers around West Berlin. Tap any point on this interactive map to see exactly where it stood and which side an address was on in 1989.
posts.alt: Where Was the Berlin Wall? An Interactive Map of East and West in 1989

posts.title: Public Toilets in Berlin: Where to Find Them, What They Cost, and Free Options
posts.summary: Need a toilet in Berlin? This tourist guide shows where to find public toilets, what they cost, where the free options are, and when stations, malls, or the Berliner Toilette app help.
posts.alt: Restroom sign with male and female symbols on a brick wall, pointing right. Green trees and glass buildings in the background.

posts.title: Berlin Address Books: How to Find Out Who Lived in Your Building
posts.alt: A row of restored late-19th-century Berlin apartment houses with ornamented stucco facades in pastel green and pink under a blue sky
posts.summary: Look up a Berlin street in the historic address books, then check which archive holds the building file.
